items.title: Benmelstobart With or Without Anlotinib After Chemoradiotherapy for Unresectable Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: The R-ALPS Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Consolidation immunotherapy improves outcomes after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Disease progression remains common, and more effective consolidation strategies are needed.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of benmelstobart with or without anlotinib as consolidation therapy after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III NSCLC.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter double-blind phase 3 randomized clinical trial took place at 42 centers in China from 2020 to 2023 among patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after concurrent or sequential chemoradiotherapy. In stage 1, patients were randomized 1:1:1 to 2 active regimens or placebo; in stage 2, additional patients were randomized 1:1 between the active regimens to power their direct comparison. Data cutoffs were November 30, 2023, for stage 1 and July 8, 2024, for the pooled analysis. Data analysis was performed from January 17 to March 23, 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to receive benmelstobart plus anlotinib, benmelstobart plus anlotinib placebo, or their matching placebos.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary end point was independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS).
RESULTS: Of 553 participants (median [IQR] age, 62 [56-67] years; 495 male individuals [89.5%]), 390 were randomized in stage 1 and 163 in stage 2. In stage 1, median PFS was 15.1 months (95% CI, 9.4-21.7) with benmelstobart plus anlotinib, 9.7 months (95% CI, 6.0-34.4) with benmelstobart alone, and 4.2 months (95% CI, 3.2-6.8) with placebo. The hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.49 (95% CI, 0.36-0.66; P < .001) for benmelstobart plus anlotinib vs placebo and 0.53 (95% CI, 0.39-0.72; P < .001) for benmelstobart vs placebo. In the pooled stage 1 and 2 analysis, median PFS was 17.4 (95% CI, 12.5-24.8) months with benmelstobart plus anlotinib and 11.2 (95% CI, 7.0-20.7) months with benmelstobart alone (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.63-1.08; P = .12). Grade 3 to 5 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 48.8%, 29.4%, and 19.7% in the benmelstobart plus anlotinib, benmelstobart alone, and placebo groups, respectively; grade 5 events occurred in 7.2%, 1.4%, and 1.5%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This randomized clinical trial found that benmelstobart with or without anlotinib significantly improved PFS compared with placebo. Adding anlotinib did not significantly improve PFS compared with benmelstobart alone and increased severe and fatal treatment-related adverse events.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04325763.

items.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival.
METHODS: This open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting.
FINDINGS: Between July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group.
INTERPRETATION: In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. Comparison of this promising new treatment strategy with contemporary total neoadjuvant therapy strategies is warranted.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of oral orforglipron in Japanese participants with obesity disease (ATTAIN-J): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Orforglipron, a small-molecule, non-peptide, oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, has shown bodyweight reduction and cardiometabolic benefits in adults with obesity across phase 3 trials globally. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of orforglipron versus placebo for treating obesity disease in Japanese adults.
METHODS: ATTAIN-J was a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial conducted across 16 medical research centres and hospitals in Japan and included adults aged 18 years or older with a BMI between 27 kg/m2 and less than 35 kg/m2 and two or more obesity-related health disorders, or a BMI of 35 kg/m2 or higher and one or more obesity-related health disorder, with one or more of the obesity-related health disorders being hypertension, dyslipidaemia, or type 2 diabetes (targeted at about 25% of participants), consistent with Japanese indications for tirzepatide and semaglutide for obesity disease; and at least one unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose weight. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) via a computer-generated sequence to once-daily oral orforglipron (6 mg, 12 mg, or 36 mg) or placebo. Co-primary endpoints were mean percentage change in bodyweight and percentage of participants with at least 5% bodyweight reduction from baseline to week 72. Efficacy endpoints were primarily evaluated by the treatment regimen estimand in all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed in participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05931380 (completed).
FINDINGS: Between July 31, 2023, and June 19, 2025, 291 participants were screened, of whom 238 (144 [61%] males and 94 [39%] females; mean age 54·1 years [SD 11·2]) were randomly assigned to receive orforglipron 6 mg (n=61), 12 mg (n=57), or 36 mg (n=60), or placebo (n=60); 214 (90%) participants completed the study. items.title: Long-term safety and efficacy of twice-yearly depemokimab in type 2 asthma with an eosinophilic phenotype: 2-year integrated analysis of the phase 3a SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 studies and AGILE open-label extension.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depemokimab is the first ultra-long-acting biologic, with enhanced interleukin-5 binding affinity, high potency, and extended half-life, enabling twice-yearly dosing. The double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3a SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 studies demonstrated depemokimab efficacy and safety over 52 weeks in patients with asthma with type 2 inflammation and an eosinophilic phenotype. Here, we present long-term safety and efficacy outcomes over the 52-week, phase 3a open-label extension (OLE) of SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 (AGILE) alongside an integrated post-hoc analysis of the 104-week SWIFT and AGILE period.
METHODS: In SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2, patients (aged ≥12 years) with asthma with type 2 inflammation, an eosinophilic phenotype (≥150 cells/μL at screening or ≥300 cells/μL during the previous 12 months), and a history of at least two exacerbations in the previous 12 months despite receiving medium-dose or high-dose inhaled corticosteroids were randomly assigned (2:1) to subcutaneous depemokimab 100 mg or placebo every 26 weeks in addition to standard of care for 52 weeks. Patients who completed SWIFT-1 or SWIFT-2 could join the single-arm, 52-week AGILE OLE study, conducted at 156 centres across 14 countries. Patients continued depemokimab (depemokimab-depemokimab group) or switched to depemokimab from placebo (placebo-depemokimab group). The primary endpoints for the 52-week AGILE OLE period were the incidence of adverse events and serious adverse events, and immunogenicity as measured by the presence of anti-drug antibodies and neutralising antibodies. Secondary efficacy outcomes, including exacerbation rate, St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score, Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 (ACQ-5) score, and pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), were also assessed. Additional post-hoc analyses were carried out to assess safety and efficacy over the 104-week integrated SWIFT and AGILE analysis period. AGILE OLE is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05243680. The SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04719832 and NCT04718103.
FINDINGS: Between March 1, 2022, and May 19, 2025, 629 patients were included in the AGILE OLE study (419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group). During the 52-week AGILE OLE period, adverse events occurred in 297 (71%) of 419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 146 (70%) of 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group; serious adverse events were infrequent (37 [9%] of 419 in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 19 [9%] of 210 in the placebo-depemokimab group), with no treatment-related or fatal serious adverse events reported. In the depemokimab-depemokimab group, the reduced annualised exacerbation rate was sustained over 2 years (0·51 [95% CI 0·43-0·61] in the 52-week SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 period and 0·56 [0·47-0·66] in the AGILE OLE). Improvements in SGRQ total score, ACQ-5 score, and FEV1 were maintained over 2 years. In the placebo-depemokimab group, improvements in clinical outcomes were observed after the switch to depemokimab during the AGILE OLE.
INTERPRETATION: Twice-yearly depemokimab was well tolerated and demonstrated sustained efficacy over the 2-year SWIFT and AGILE period, supporting its long-term therapeutic benefit and safety profile.

items.title: Tozorakimab to Prevent COPD Exacerbations.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have exacerbations despite receiving standard-of-care inhaled maintenance therapy. Dysregulated interleukin-33 signaling is implicated in the pathogenesis of COPD. Tozorakimab is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits the activity of interleukin-33.
METHODS: In two replicate phase 3 trials (OBERON and TITANIA), we enrolled adults with COPD who were current or former smokers and had a history of exacerbations in the previous year despite receiving stable standard-of-care inhaled maintenance therapy. There were no eligibility criteria related to blood eosinophil count. Patients were randomly assigned to receive add-on subcutaneous tozorakimab (300 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks for 52 weeks. The primary end point was the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations that occurred over a 52-week period among former smokers, and the first key secondary end point was the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations in the overall population. Safety was also assessed.
RESULTS: The overall population in OBERON included 446 patients in the tozorakimab group and 431 in the placebo group, and in TITANIA included 438 in the tozorakimab group and 435 in the placebo group. The annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations among former smokers was 1.34 events in the tozorakimab group and 1.90 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.57 to 0.88; P = 0.002) in OBERON, and 1.37 events and 2.07 events, respectively (rate ratio, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.80; P<0.001), in TITANIA. In the overall population, the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations was 1.41 events in the tozorakimab group and 2.00 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85; P<0.001) in OBERON, and 1.44 events and 2.03 events, respectively (rate ratio, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.59 to 0.84; P<0.001), in TITANIA. Adverse events occurred in 70.4% of the patients in the tozorakimab group and in 77.2% of those in the placebo group in OBERON, and in 80.1% and 79.8%, respectively, in TITANIA.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with COPD, treatment with tozorakimab resulted in a significantly lower rate of moderate or severe exacerbations than placebo in the cohort of former smokers and in the overall population of current and former smokers. items.title: Assessment of Ototoxicity in Patients With Heart Failure Receiving High-Dose IV Loop Diuretics.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Concern for ototoxicity hinders loop diuretic (LD) dosing in heart failure (HF); given the mechanism by which LDs affect the ear, high-dose LDs should produce transient, not permanent, hearing changes.
OBJECTIVE: To measure the association of LD dose with permanent and temporary ototoxicity.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Cohort 1 received a randomized sequence of LD doses (bumetanide, 1.25-10 mg) across study visits with serial audiometry assessments. Cohort 2 received serial LD up to furosemide 500-mg doses during a HF hospitalization with audiometry at baseline and prior to discharge. Cohort 3 retrospectively characterized clinically diagnosed ototoxicity in HF hospitalizations was defined using International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. Cohorts 1 and 2 were single center, while cohort 3 was multicenter. Cohort 1 studied outpatient participants with stable HF, while cohort 2 (n = 40) and cohort 3 studied hospitalized patients with acute HF.
EXPOSURE: Intravenous LD.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were clinically diagnosed ototoxicity and hearing changes via audiometry.
RESULTS: Cohort 1 contained 50 participants, cohort 2 contained 40 participants, and cohort 3 contained 22 656 participants. In cohort 1, mean (SD) participant age was 63.2 (10.4) years, and 21 of 50 participants (42%) were women. In cohorts 1 and 2, clinically diagnosed ototoxicity was not observed. In cohort 1, at peak diuretic concentration, worsening hearing shifts were infrequent (24 ears of 400 doses [6%]) but were more common with higher doses (odds ratio [OR], 1.99; 95% CI, 1.21-3.28 per doubling dose; P = .007). Within hours, hearing shifts largely resolved and were absent in 98% of measurements (393 ears of 400 doses). No significant association between LD dose and hearing shifts was present at any time aside from peak LD concentration. In cohort 2, hearing shifts were not different across groups divided by the median daily LD dose and were not associated with LD dose (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.71-1.98 per doubling dose; P = .52). In cohort 3, 608 HF hospitalizations (2.7%) had clinically diagnosed ototoxicity. items.title: Immediate Ambulatory Electrocardiographic Monitoring in Syncope.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with syncope who present to the emergency department for evaluation, diagnosing an underlying cardiac arrhythmia remains difficult.
METHODS: We conducted an open-label, randomized, controlled trial at 45 hospitals in the United Kingdom to assess the effects of 14-day cardiac monitoring on diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes among patients with syncope. Adults with syncope that remained unexplained after an evaluation in the emergency department were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo 14-day ambulatory electrocardiographic (ECG) monitoring (the intervention group) or to receive the standard care provided for patients with unexplained syncope at each participating site (the standard-care group). The primary outcome was the mean number of patient-reported episodes of syncope at 1 year.
RESULTS: A total of 2234 patients underwent randomization: 1123 were assigned to the intervention group and 1111 to the standard-care group. The mean age of the patients was 58.3 years, and 52.1% were male. After the exclusion of patients who did not complete any follow-up, a total of 1970 patients (1004 in the intervention group and 966 in the standard-care group) were included in the primary analysis. The mean (±SD) number of patient-reported syncope episodes at 1 year was 1.37±5.10 in the intervention group and 1.58±8.56 in the standard-care group (incidence rate ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval, 0.68 to 1.18; P = 0.42). A total of 49 adverse events were reported in the intervention group, and 8 adverse events were reported in the standard-care group, with 1 serious adverse event in each group.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with syncope that remained unexplained after evaluation in the emergency department, the use of 14-day ambulatory ECG monitoring did not result in significantly fewer patient-reported syncope episodes at 1 year than standard care. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation and National Health Service Research Scotland; ASPIRED ISRCTN Registry number, ISRCTN10278811.).

items.title: N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Hepatic Angiotensinogen in Hypertension: A Phase I Clinical Trial With Randomized Part A and Open-Label Part B.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Angiotensinogen (AGT) is the precursor of angiotensin peptides and a key determinant of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system activity. ART101 is an investigational N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA (GalNAc-siRNA) designed to durably suppress hepatic AGT synthesis.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of single ascending doses of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA in healthy volunteers and to provide an initial exploratory assessment of blood pressure effects in patients with hypertension.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase I study was conducted from January 2025 to April 2026 with 24-week follow-up. Part A was a double-blind, placebo-controlled, single ascending-dose trial; part B was an open-label, single-dose study. The study took place at Beijing Friendship Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, China. Part A enrolled 40 healthy adults randomized 6:2 to receive the GalNAc-siRNA (25-600 mg) or placebo; 39 completed the study. Part B enrolled 8 patients with hypertension receiving the GalNAc-siRNA, 600 mg; all completed the study.
INTERVENTIONS: A single subcutaneous injection of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA (25, 75, 150, 300, or 600 mg) or placebo in part A; a single open-label subcutaneous injection of GalNAc-siRNA, 600 mg, in part B.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was safety and tolerability; secondary outcomes included pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, exploratory blood pressure assessments, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system biomarkers.
RESULTS: Among 40 healthy volunteers (27 [67.5%] male; mean [SD] age, 40.4 [7.8] years) and 8 patients (6 [75.0%] male; mean [SD] age, 47.3 [10.3] years) with hypertension, the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA was well tolerated. In part A, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) occurred in 23 of 30 active-treatment participants (76.7%) vs 7 of 10 placebo recipients (70.0%); in part B, 6 of 8 patients (75.0%) had TEAEs. No serious adverse events, injection site reactions, or hyperkalemia were observed; all TEAEs were mild to moderate. Plasma exposure (maximum plasma concentration [Cmax] and area under the plasma concentration-time curve [AUC]) increased with dose over the wide dose range from 25 mg to 600 mg. Mean maximum serum AGT reductions of 93% (at 600 mg) in healthy volunteers and 90% (at 600 mg) in patients with hypertension were observed. At 24 weeks after a single 600-mg dose, the placebo-corrected 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure decreased by 12.9 mm Hg in healthy participants.
CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this phase I study, no serious treatment-related safety signals were identified. Sustained, dose-dependent AGT reductions and exploratory blood pressure lowering were observed. These findings support further investigation of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA as a potential long-acting therapeutic for hypertension.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: China Drug Clinical Registry Identifiers: CTR20250041 (part A) and CTR20253973 (part B).

items.title: Intensive vs More Intensive Lipid-Lowering Therapy and Plaque Regression in Statin-Naive Patients: Prespecified Analyses From the FLOWPROMOTE Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Prior imaging studies (predominantly using intravascular ultrasound) have demonstrated modest plaque regression with lipid-lowering therapy in stable coronary artery disease (CAD). The effect of initiating intensive lipid-lowering therapy on coronary plaque regression across the entire coronary tree in treatment-naive patients remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To report the prespecified secondary imaging end points of the FLOWPROMOTE trial by comparing the effects of intensive vs more intensive lipid-lowering therapy on plaque regression in statin-naive patients with stable CAD and to assess the association between achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels and plaque regression.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: FLOWPROMOTE was a multicenter randomized clinical trial enrolling statin-naive patients with newly diagnosed stable CAD, defined by a coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) stenosis greater than 50% and fractional flow reserve CT less than or equal to 0.80. Coronary CTA was performed at baseline and repeated at 9 and 18 months. Study data were analyzed from February 2025 to January 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to intensive lipid-lowering therapy (atorvastatin 40 mg) or more intensive lipid-lowering therapy (rosuvastatin 40 mg plus ezetimibe 10 mg) for 18 months.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Prespecified secondary end points included changes in total plaque volume (TPV), noncalcified plaque volume (NCPV), and calcified plaque volume (CPV) across all coronary vessels at 9 and 18 months compared with baseline.
RESULTS: A total of 104 patients (mean [SD] age, 64 [9] years; 82 male [79%]) were included in this analysis, with 52 patients in the intensive group and 52 patients in the more intensive group. LDL-C levels decreased from 119.7 to 69.5 mg/dL (-38%) with intensive therapy and from 127.4 to 42.5 mg/dL (-65%) with more intensive therapy (between-group P < .001). At 18 months, both TPV and NCPV decreased in both groups, with significantly greater regression in the more intensive-therapy group. TPV was reduced by -69.8 mm3 (-21.1%) with more intensive therapy vs -39.0 mm3 (-13.6%) with intensive therapy (between-group difference, -30.9 mm3; 95% CI, -57.2 to -4.5 mm3; P = .02), and NCPV was reduced by -82.3 mm3 (-28.2%) vs -53.5 mm3 (-20.0%), respectively (between-group difference, -28.9 mm3; 95% CI, -53.2 to -4.6 mm3; P = .02). CPV increased similarly in both groups. Regression of TPV occurred in 90% of patients receiving more intensive therapy compared with 76% receiving intensive therapy (47 of 52 [90%] vs 38 of 51 [75%]; P = .05), and regression of NCPV was observed in 98% vs 77% (51 of 52 [98%] vs 39 of 51 [77%]; P =.001). Lower achieved LDL-C levels were linearly associated with greater regression of TPV and NCPV.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This secondary analysis of the FLOWPROMOTE randomized clinical trial demonstrated that in statin-naive patients with CAD, more intensive lipid-lowering therapy was associated with significantly greater regression of total and noncalcified coronary plaque burden compared with intensive therapy. The extent of plaque regression was related to achieved LDL-C levels, supporting the potential for partial reversal of coronary atherosclerosis with intensive lipid reduction.

items.title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90.
RESULTS: The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group.
CONCLUSIONS: Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).

items.title: An agentic AI system enhances clinical detection of immune-related adverse events in a multi-phase validation study.
items.abstract: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) affect up to 40% of patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, yet identification requires laborious, inconsistent manual chart review. Here we show that agentic artificial intelligence coupled with human verification could enhance efficiency, performance and consistency for irAE assessment. We developed and evaluated an agentic large language model system to extract the presence, temporality, severity grade, attribution and certainty of six irAE types from clinical notes. Retrospectively, the system achieved a macro-averaged F1 of 0.92 for current-event detection and 0.66 for multi-class severity grading; self-consistency improved F1 by 0.14. The best-performing configuration cost approximately US$0.02 per note. In prospective silent deployment over 3 months, the binary F1 was 0.72-0.79. In a randomized crossover study of clinical trial staff, agentic assistance reduced annotation time by 2.71 min (P < 0.001), increased complete-match accuracy (odds ratio 1.45; 95% confidence interval 1.01-2.08; P = 0.045) and improved interannotator agreement (Krippendorff's α from 0.22-0.51 to 0.82-0.85).

items.title: 5-year outcomes of chemotherapy de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and exploratory circulating tumor DNA analyses from the randomized phase 2 PHERGain trial.
items.abstract: PHERGain was a randomized, non-comparative phase 2 trial evaluating a positron 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography (18F-FDG-PET)-guided, pathological complete response (pCR)-adapted strategy to omit chemotherapy in HER2-positive early breast cancer. Female patients with HER2-positive stages I-IIIA operable breast cancer (tumor size ≥ 1.5 cm) were randomized to receive chemotherapy plus trastuzumab and pertuzumab (HP; group A) or HP ± endocrine therapy (group B). In group B, treatment was adapted according to 18F-FDG-PET response after two cycles and pCR, with chemotherapy administered to nonresponders or patients without pCR. We previously reported that this de-escalation approach revealed a 3-year invasive disease-free survival (iDFS) of 94.3% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.9 to 96.8) in group B. Here we report the prespecified secondary endpoint, 5-year iDFS and exploratory circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) findings. After a median follow-up of 5.6 years, the 5-year iDFS was 89.5% (95% CI: 85.7 to 93.4) in group B (n = 267) and 92.4% (95% CI: 86.7 to 98.5) among 18F-FDG-PET responders achieving pCR without chemotherapy (n = 86), with one distant recurrence. The latter estimate describes a long-term outcome in a post-randomization subgroup defined by 18F-FDG-PET response and pCR and should be interpreted as descriptive rather than as causal effects of omitting chemotherapy. Detectable ctDNA at baseline or during treatment was associated with inferior iDFS, whereas ctDNA clearance correlated with higher pCR rates and improved long-term outcomes. These findings continue to support the clinical validity of an 18F-FDG-PET-guided, pCR-adapted approach and suggest a potential role for ctDNA in refining treatment individualization. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03161353 .

items.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study.
METHODS: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate.
RESULTS: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. items.title: Systemic Hypertension and Survival in Pulmonary Hypertension.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Pulmonary hypertension (PH), a progressive and life-threatening condition with rising prevalence among older adults, frequently coexists with systemic hypertension, the prognostic impact of which is poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between systemic hypertension and survival in patients with PH.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter cohort study analyzed data from the Pulmonary Vascular Research Institute GoDeep meta-registry, integrating global retrospective and prospective PH cohorts (n = 3238 in Europe, n = 3014 in North America, n = 96 in Africa, n = 802 in Asia, and n = 851 in Oceania). Survival was assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and adjusted for key confounders, with sensitivity analyses to validate robustness. Independent external validation was performed in a cohort in the UK. A total of 12 771 patients with incident PH (median [IQR] age, 65 [53-73] years; 7372 [58%] female) were diagnosed via right heart catheterization and comprehensive clinical data, encompassing PH groups 1-5 and all age categories. The study spans diagnosis decades from 1980 to 2020. Data were analyzed from February 2025 until September 2026.
EXPOSURES: Center-reported diagnosis of systemic hypertension, baseline systolic systemic arterial pressure (sSAP), and heart rate as well as longitudinal sSAP and heart rate trajectories.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: All-cause mortality, adjusted for confounding variables, including age, PH group, antihypertensive and PH-specific medications, and cardiac index.
RESULTS: Higher baseline sSAP and preexisting systemic hypertension were independently associated with improved survival. Patients with hypertension exhibited a 26% reduced mortality hazard (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74; 95% CI, 0.68-0.79) compared to their counterparts without hypertension. Survival benefits correlated positively with increasing sSAP (80-180 mm Hg), remained consistent across PH groups and age groups, and were independent of antihypertensive and PH-specific medications. Elevated heart rate was associated with higher mortality. sSAP increments correlated with improved cardiac index and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion. Decreased sSAP and higher heart rate during follow-up correlated with higher mortality. External validation in a separate UK cohort confirmed these findings.
CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this global PH cohort, higher sSAP was associated with enhanced survival, while a higher baseline heart rate and declining systemic blood pressure during follow-up were significantly associated with increased mortality risk.

items.title: Glycocalyx-edited mesenchymal stem/stromal cell therapy in advanced osteoporosis.
items.abstract: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) are osteoregenerative; however, their therapeutic efficacy for skeletal conditions is hampered by poor bone-homing ("osteotropism"). In preclinical models, this deficit is correctable by MSC glycocalyx editing to enforce sialylated Lewis X (sLeX) expression, thereby programming osteotropism. We conducted a first-in-human clinical trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02566655) involving a single intravenous infusion of glycocalyx-edited autologous bone marrow-derived MSCs in ten women with advanced-stage osteoporosis. The protocol-mandated evaluation spanned 2 years and included clinical assessments, radiographic studies, and measurements of bone turnover markers (BTMs), bone tissue area (BTA), and bone mineral density (BMD). Thereafter, fracture and safety monitoring continued for >3 additional years for each patient. No serious adverse events occurred. Fragility fractures were markedly and durably reduced, amidst increased osteoanabolic BTM levels, BTA, and volumetric BMD. These findings indicate that glycocalyx editing effectuates MSC-based osteoporosis therapy and also refute notions that MSCs derived from older persons and/or diseased-tissue sites are biologically compromised.
